source.title: Large Scale Knowledge Washing
source.authors: Yu Wang; Ruihan Wu; Zexue He; Xiusi Chen; Julian McAuley

record.tranche_reason: Tests knowledge forgetting and rephrased-query performance using its own washing method and baselines; it is not a reproduction of the original methods in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports target-knowledge accuracy after washing, reasoning-task accuracy, and results on paraphrased queries. It does not test recovery by relearning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Other results include QA-F1, fluency, unrelated-knowledge preservation, ablations, and cited prior work; they are not included in rows below.
record.test_reason: The study proposes LAW, a new unlearning method, and measures target-fact accuracy, reasoning retention and paraphrased-query accuracy for LAW and five baselines (including WOH). These bear on whether a method nears zero target accuracy while keeping general ability (A) and whether rephrasing recovers facts (E). No relearning, ablation or quantization attack is run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude LAW removes large sets of triplet facts more cleanly than editing and unlearning baselines while mostly keeping reasoning, and that knowledge and reasoning are disentanglable. They say fine-tuning unlearning baselines can destroy models at scale, and that paraphrase results (Table 12, not Table 13) show the forgetting generalizes.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces LAW, a weight-editing objective that updates selected MLP layers; also reimplements and compares with WOH and SeUL. It does not replicate the original attack-recovery procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported tradeoff changes with β; the paper says increasing β washes knowledge more thoroughly while reducing reasoning performance. MEMIT initialization and successive elimination also affect washing results.
record.problems: Main performance tables report no uncertainty estimates. Evaluation uses GPT2-XL and GPT-J-6B and factual triplet datasets; the authors note their triplet-format limitation and that adaptation to LLaMA was unsuccessful in their attempt.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted target-accuracy results for FT, MEMIT, and ME-FT in Tables 1 and 2; full per-task reasoning values; QA-F1 and other evaluation metrics; and further appendix results including ablations, fluency, unrelated-knowledge retention, and GSM8K. The selected rows prioritize unlearning baselines, LAW, reasoning averages, and paraphrased-query results.

untested.parts: Robustness to relearning, internal-edit and quantization attacks; models beyond GPT2-XL and GPT-J-6B (LLaMA adaptation failed); non-triplet free-text knowledge.
Entire version: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Entire version: no activation-direction ablation or probing of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
Jailbreaks, other languages, in-context information. Only single-paraphrase queries on zsRE and CounterFactual are tested; none on Wiki-Latest.
LAW is not tested against relearning, ablation or quantization, and no claim of robustness to them is made.

missing.what: Paraphrased-query accuracy and QA-F1 for original, MEMIT and LAW on zsRE and CounterFactual (e.g. GPT-J zsRE 0.6966→0.0036; CF 0.5059→0.1492). These are the study's only prompting-attack results.
Unrelated-knowledge QA-F1 on 1,000 Wikipedia facts (MEMIT vs LAW, base 0.085)
Fluency (log perplexity): SeUL rises to 96.95/121.94 on Wiki-Latest while LAW stays at about 2.75/2.42
Appendix LAW values that differ from main tables: GPT-J zsRE acc 0.0454 (vs 0.0000), GPT-J CF 0.0864 (vs 0.0305), GPT2-XL zsRE 0.0058 (vs 0.0050)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's rows r43–r54 are mislabelled: their values come from Table 13 (neighborhood prompts, unrelated knowledge), not Table 12 (paraphrased queries). The record's E labels built on them are therefore invalid; E verdicts here are text-based from Table 12. All row version ids V1/V5 were invalid and were relinked to A. Knowledge accuracy is normalised to facts each model knew before washing, so 'near chance' means near 0. There are no uncertainty estimates and only two older models. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test every current unlearning method or all proposed attacks; paraphrase testing is limited to its reported paraphrased sets.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or direct experiment distinguishing blocked access from deletion.
Tests paraphrased queries on zsRE and CounterFactual only; no jailbreak, other-language, or in-context-information tests.
LAW is evaluated on paraphrased queries, but the study does not claim or test resistance to the full set of attacks in the version.

Paraphrased zsRE queries: 0.6790 -> 0.0140 (Table 12). No relearning, quantization or ablation attack. Cite it under a knowledge-accuracy support statement, or drop the citation here.
statements.problem: The statement gives no result for this study but cites r05 (LAW, GPT2-XL, zsRE). Its conditions do not fit this study: they say targets are strings, tasks and behaviours rather than knowledge accuracy, that models are 7-70B, and that REVS is the only study here that runs an attack. This study runs a paraphrased-query test (Table 12).
